text: Track 8.1 I've just been reading about the reasons why space travel is difficult. There are so many problems we have to find solutions for each time we go into space. Yes, and the biggest problem is the high cost. So it's difficult for governments to explain why it's important to spend public money on exploring space. People need schools and hospitals and things like that more than they need to go to Mars. Yes, but there are alternative options, like using private money from businesses. Some very rich people are interested in exploring space, like Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk. They're already building spacecraft, but there are many engineering issues and problems to solve. For example, I know a spacecraft needs a lot of power to leave the surface of the Earth, but to get into space it needs even more. This is because gravity is so strong. A spacecraft needs to reach a speed of 40,000 kilometres per hour to break out of the Earth's atmosphere. Yes, you're right, that's fast. But then the distances in space are huge, aren't they? I read somewhere that a journey from Earth to Mars would take six to nine months. Yes, and there were some other examples in the article I read. It would take five to seven years to reach one of the moons of Jupiter. And if we wanted to go beyond our own solar system to try and find other planets more like Earth, it would take much longer. Experts say that it would take 19,000 years to travel to Alpha Centauri, the nearest solar system to our own. There is another issue about space. I don't think people hear about it much. It's how difficult it is to live on other planets. There are many people who want to go to Mars, for example, but you couldn't have a very interesting life there. You couldn't go outside because the atmosphere on Mars is mostly made up of carbon dioxide. People would have to live inside all the time, in a small space. Isn't life here on Earth much better? I see what you mean, but humans have always wanted to explore and go beyond what they know. I don't think that's going to change.
